purpose: Lets an agent work out whether the skills on its machine differ from this repository without reading every file. Compare 'version' and each file 'sha' against the local clone. Authority is always the SKILL.md files themselves; this manifest is an index, not a contract.

versioning.rule: There are no invented version numbers. A skill's 'version' is the short hash of the last commit that touched its directory, and 'updated' is that commit's date. A skill whose files have not changed keeps the same version, even when the repository moves on.
versioning.verify_file_sha: git -C <repo> ls-files -s workspace/.claude/skills/<name>/<file>   # column 2 is the sha below
versioning.sha_meaning: git blob sha of the file's content. Two clones with the same sha have byte-identical files. A different sha means the file was changed on one side — it does not say which side.
versioning.note: 'lines' is a convenience for spotting large divergence at a glance. It is not authoritative; the sha is.
versioning.regenerate_when: Any file under skills_root is added, removed or changed — in the same commit as that change, not afterwards. 'generated_from_commit' is how a reader tells whether this file has fallen behind: if it is not the tip of main, treat every entry below as a claim about an older state of the repository.
versioning.am_i_stale: git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD   # if this does not equal generated_from_commit, this manifest describes an older commit than the clone it is sitting in. Run it before you trust anything below.
versioning.authoritative_file_list: git -C <repo> ls-files -s workspace/.claude/skills/   # this, not the 'skills' array, is the truth about which files exist and what their shas are. Where the two disagree, git wins and this file is the bug.
versioning.unlisted_files_on_disk: A file present under a skill directory but absent from that skill's 'files' array means one of two things, and they need opposite responses. Either this manifest is stale (check am_i_stale, and check `git -C <repo> log --oneline -1 -- <path>` — if the file is tracked, it is ours and the manifest simply fell behind), or the file is untracked and is the person's own addition. In neither case is deleting it correct. Surface it and say which of the two it is.
versioning.referenced_but_not_present_scope: Verified against generated_from_commit by resolving every backticked file path in each SKILL.md. Paths containing a date placeholder (YYYY-MM-DD) or a name placeholder ({name}, {project-name}, {slug}) are created at runtime and are deliberately excluded — their absence from a fresh clone is normal. Re-verify with: grep -o '`[^`]*\.\(md\|py\|sh\)`' <SKILL.md>

how_to_diff: For a single skill: git -C <repo> log --oneline HEAD..origin/main -- workspace/.claude/skills/<name>/
Do not act on a difference by overwriting. See UPDATING.md.

not_shipped.note: Present in .gitignore, therefore absent from every fresh clone, but referenced by the skills below. Create them locally; do not add them to git.

locally_modified_by_design.note: These are tracked by git and are also rewritten by the first-run setup wizard with the person's real content. That makes them permanently modified in every working install, which is what makes updates awkward. UPDATING.md section 5 is about exactly these two files. Never restore, reset or overwrite them to match this repository.

skills.name: audio-transcribe
requires: A recording. Nothing here produces audio.
An API key on a free tier, in the person's own account: Groq for en/zh, Gemini for km. tools/setup-api-key.sh takes it without the value passing through the conversation.
ffmpeg, for recordings over 25 MB and for the Khmer route.
Scripts live in workspace/tools/ and are reached only through tools/transcribe.sh.
skills.known_inconsistency: The Skills Index row for this skill in workspace/CLAUDE.md was rewritten upstream again on 2026-08-29, to describe the four-file shape (references/QA.md + human/), and a voiceink row was added below it. CONSEQUENCE FOR EXISTING CLONES: workspace/CLAUDE.md is listed under locally_modified_by_design, so this upstream change WILL collide with a person's own edits. Do NOT resolve that by overwriting their file — follow UPDATING.md section 5: fetch first, back up, show the person the difference, keep their lines.
skills.notes: Restructured on 2026-08-29 (aa8a8c3) into the four-file standard: INSTALL.md, FLOW.md, VERIFY.md and the old top-level QA.md folded into SKILL.md and references/QA.md, and the teaching/audio-transcribe/ pages retired in the same commit. A clone made before that date loses those eight files on its next pull; that is expected, see UPDATING.md section 4. The human/ pages are Traditional Chinese on purpose. Earlier history: rewritten 2026-08-04 from 368 lines to 79, with references/ and templates/ removed then — the same rule applied.

skills.name: plan-discuss

skills.notes: Frontmatter sets disable-model-invocation: true, deliberately. Read the file and follow it; do not call it as a tool. In some harnesses this also removes it from the skill listing, which is not a missing skill.

skills.name: voiceink
requires: VoiceInk itself, on Apple Silicon with macOS 14.4+. Installing it, granting the three permissions, and downloading the model are GUI steps the person does at their own screen — no script here can do them.
Nothing in this skill runs code on the person's machine. The payload is pasted into the app by the person; verification is them dictating and pasting the raw output back.
skills.notes: First skill born into the four-file standard (2026-08-29). The payload blocks in SKILL.md are verbatim Traditional Chinese from the field-tested source and are the point of the skill — a diff that 'tidies' them is wrong. UI positions are stated against VoiceInk v1.79 (released 2026-05-23); the file itself says the app in front of you wins.
